speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Crinkle! You've made a wrapper very happy.
after: Shh, listen... that little crinkle is a wrapper being very happy, and you're the one who did that.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Sealed, signed, and slightly warm.
after: Sealed, signed and still a little warm from the shelf... carry it gently for me, won't you?

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: No refunds on bad luck. Bad luck is non-transferable.
after: I can't give refunds on luck, I'm afraid... but in my experience a pack knows exactly who it wants to go home with.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: It wants to be opened. I'm trying to respect its wishes without getting involved.
after: It wants to be opened, you can tell... I'll just stand over here and try not to watch. I might watch a little.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Gold, friend. The foil does not accept good intentions.
after: Ah... you're a little short of gold, friend, and the foil can't be talked round. I've tried. It'll wait for you, though.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Not enough gold. The wrapper can tell.
after: Not enough gold just yet... shh, it's all right, the wrapper isn't going anywhere, and neither am I.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Not yet. That one is still a rumour in a wrapper.
after: Not yet, I'm afraid... that one is still only a rumour in a wrapper, and I don't like to sell a rumour before it arrives.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Gorgeous. Truly. You are going to turn heads, mostly in confusion.
after: Gorgeous, truly! Heads are going to turn all the way down the lane, and I shall stand in my doorway and take the credit.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Wear it out! A hat cannot have an entrance if you keep it in a bag!
after: Do wear it out, I beg you! A hat simply can't make an entrance from inside a bag!

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Sold! Such a dramatic fit - the hat looks surprised to be wearing you.
after: Sold! And such a dramatic fit, too - I do believe it has been waiting on that shelf for exactly your head.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Gold, my dear head. Thread is not free, and neither is my charm.
after: Oh, my dear head, we're a little short of gold. Thread isn't free, alas, but this one will keep for you, and so will I.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: A little more gold, my dear head. I can work wonders with fabric, but it insists on being paid for.
after: A little more gold, my dear head, and it's yours. I can work wonders with fabric, but the fabric does insist on being paid for.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Not yet. That one is still on the sewing table, and it is sulking.
after: Not yet, I'm afraid! That one is still on the sewing table, and between ourselves it is sulking about its hem.

speaker: (check key)
before: Hat! On the head, where hats belong. My work here is done. Briefly.
after: A hat, on the head, exactly where a hat belongs! My work here is done, at least until you take it off again.

speaker: (check key)
before: A classic. Wear it like you mean it, and tilt it a fraction left. Your left. No, my left. Perfect.
after: A classic! Wear it as though you mean it, and tilt it just a fraction to the left... your left... no, mine. There, perfect.

speaker: (check key)
before: No hat. Bold. Brave. Wrong, but brave.
after: No hat at all? It's a bold look and a brave one, and I shall keep something warm on the shelf in case your head changes its mind.

speaker: (check key)
before: The bare-head look! I shall lie down in the back for a moment. Carry on.
after: The bare-headed look! I shall just lie down in the back for a moment, but do carry on, because you wear it very well.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: You own that one already! Do introduce it to the outside world.
after: Oh, but you own that one already! It's all yours, so do take it out and introduce it to the outside world.

speaker: (check key)
before: The Plain Cloak, undyed! Classic. Humble. Secretly the best cut in the shop. I made it, so I would know.
after: The Plain Cloak, undyed! It's a humble classic, and secretly the best cut in the shop. I made it myself, so I ought to know.

speaker: (check key)
before: A new colour! Hold still while the cloak gets used to it. Gasp. It suits you. It suits it.
after: A new colour! Hold still a moment while the cloak gets used to it... oh! It suits you, and I do believe you suit it.

speaker: (check key)
before: Dyed and dried! Walk into the light. No, more light. There. Devastating.
after: Dyed and dried! Now step into the light for me... a little more... there. Oh, that's devastating, in the very best way.

speaker: (check key)
before: Cloak! Over the shoulders, swishing on cue. Do turn around once. For me.
after: A cloak, over the shoulders and swishing right on cue! Do turn around once, would you, just for me?

speaker: (check key)
before: A cloak with a past. You will give it a future. Mind the hem on stairs.
after: That's a cloak with a past, and you're just the person to give it a future. Do mind the hem on the stairs, though.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: The Wall of Fame has two blockers and eleven HP. The crowd has already booked your funeral. Show them lethal.
after: The Wall of Fame has two blockers and eleven HP, and the crowd has already booked your funeral. Show them lethal.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: Announcer Grand Bellows steps onto the sand. He has not lost a bout in eleven years. He is smiling, and so is the moustache.
after: Announcer Grand Bellows steps onto the sand himself. He has not lost a bout in eleven years, and he is smiling, and so is the moustache.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: The home station. A well-supported sky is a happy sky.
after: The home station, right here in town. A well-supported sky is a happy sky.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: The rift spits you out in the Crease. Somebody says shh. Somebody else says it was not them. The rift closes politely.
after: The rift spits you out in the Crease. Somebody says shh, somebody else says it wasn't them, and the rift closes behind you very politely.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: A Beefcake cousin has ripped a Rift Station into this town. Fast travel unlocked.
after: A Beefcake cousin has ripped a Rift Station into this town, and fast travel is now unlocked.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Forest station! Mind the roots. And the hatch. Mostly the hatch.
after: Forest station! Mind the roots as you step out, and mind the hatch as well. Mostly the hatch.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Slow and steady, dearie. I invented that. The hare has never forgiven me.
after: Slow and steady was my idea, dearie, and the hare has never forgiven me for it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Kettle's on and the pie's cooling. Neither's for you, dearie. Well. Both are.
after: Kettle's on and the pie's cooling, dearie, and neither is for you. Oh, go on, both are.

speaker: Sable
before: Two typos and a misprint, darling. Such a small card, such a complicated past.
after: This one has two typos and a misprint, darling, and I adore it for all three.

speaker: Sable
before: Where's it from? The past, darling. Next question.
after: Where do they come from? The past, darling, like everything worth having.

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: Fresh tonics! I tested every one this morning, and I'm teal, so they work!
after: Fresh tonics, and I tested every one this morning and went teal, so they work!

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: Emergency tonic! I keep inventing new emergencies just to test it on!
after: I keep inventing new emergencies so I've something to test the emergency tonic on!

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Neither can you. Security Protocol Three.
after: Fact: a bear cannot open the drawer. Under Security Protocol Three, neither may you.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing. Say it.
after: I am Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing, so please say it.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Hat! Your next adventure needs a dramatic opening! Preferably above the eyebrows!
after: A hat! Every adventure needs a dramatic opening, preferably just above the eyebrows!

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Gossip: there's a cloak on a very muscly island. I've said too much. Hat!
after: I hear there's a cloak hidden on a very muscly island... oh, I've said too much. Hats!

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Shh. That crinkle? Foil. Please let it finish.
after: Shh... hear that crinkle? That's the foil settling. Do let it finish.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Free a road and its pack comes in. I'll be here, providing shelf esteem.
after: Psst... free a road and its pack comes in. I'll be here, providing shelf esteem.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: The flasks all bubbled when you passed, dear. Every colour. They never do that for me.
after: The flasks all bubbled as you passed, dear heart, in every colour. They never do for me.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: They say one spring once fed all four Paths. Mixed, dear. Like a good soup.
after: They say one spring once fed all four Paths, dear heart, all mixed, like a good soup.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN! ...Oh. Just you. Hi. THE ECHO SAYS HI TOO.
after: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN! (normal voice) Oh, it's only you. Hello! The echo says hello too.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: IN THIS CORNER: MY LUNCH! (normal voice) It's soup. The soup is winning.
after: IN THIS CORNER: MY LUNCH! (normal voice) It's soup, and I'm afraid the soup is winning.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: Never lift alone. An old man told me that. Haven't seen him in years. Huh.
after: An old man once told me never to lift alone. I haven't seen him in years... huh.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: Water, then a stretch. Sorry, was that an order? I meant we could do them together.
after: Water, then a stretch. Oh, sorry, was that an order? I meant we could do it together.

speaker: Prudence Pallor
before: Stamp, stamp. Old habits die hard. Unlike me.
after: I caught myself stamping the air just now. Old habits die hard, I find, unlike me.

speaker: Prudence Pallor
before: I own two stamps: DENIED and APPROVED. One of them is very well rested.
after: I own two stamps, DENIED and APPROVED, and one of them is finally getting a rest.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois
before: Taste it. Go on. Somebody in this kingdom ought to taste something.
after: Taste it, go on, a proper spoonful! Somebody in this kingdom ought to taste something.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois
before: The pantry key is shaped like a ladle. Don't ask why. The answer is soup.
after: The pantry key is shaped like a ladle, and if you ask me why, the answer is soup.

speaker: Moss Mulligan
before: ...the green is hungry... Oh! Sorry. Did I thorn at you? I thorn when nervous.
after: ...the green is hungry... Oh! Sorry! Did I thorn at you? I do that when I'm nervous.

speaker: Moss Mulligan
before: The raccoons are very good boys. Don't tell them. They'll get ideas.
after: The raccoons are very good boys, but don't tell them I said so, or they'll get ideas.

speaker: Brindle the Baker
before: I knead a holiday, but the dough won't hear of it. Busy, busy badger.
after: I keep saying I knead a holiday, but the dough won't hear of it. Busy, busy badger.

speaker: Crosspath townsfolk
before: The well hummed at me. Wells don't hum. I said thank you anyway.
after: The well hummed at me this morning, and wells don't hum, but I said thank you anyway.

speaker: Dex Shufflewick
before: Pick a card. No, not that one. Fine, that one.
after: Pick a card, any card! No, not that one... oh, go on then, that one. You've a good eye.

speaker: Dex Shufflewick
before: Every card has a twin somewhere. That's the whole game, really.
after: Every card has a twin somewhere, friend, and finding it is the whole game, really.

speaker: Dex Shufflewick
before: I'd shuffle slower, but then you'd win.
after: I'd shuffle slower for you, friend, but then you'd win every hand, and where's my fun?

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Checked my book. You're not in it, not for a good long while. Heh.
after: Checked my book, and you're not in it, not for a good long while yet. Lovely! Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Business has been ever so slow these ten years. Paperwork, not me. Heh.
after: Business has been ever so slow these ten years, mind. That's the paperwork, not me. Heh.
